boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented George Mason rituals, recurring events, and campus objects that connect orientation, student life, and graduation.

cards.title: Leave Your Name on Your Class Sign
cards.subtitle: An orientation ritual displayed across the Fairfax Campus
cards.notes: Find the sign for your entering year during orientation and add your name; photograph the accumulating signatures before leaving.
cards.short_summary: Each entering class turns a large year sign into a collective record of its arrival at George Mason.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason's 2026–2027 New Student Guide directs students to find the class sign matching the year they started and add their name.
cards.access_notes: The guide identifies this as a student tradition associated with the year a student entered George Mason.

cards.title: Rub George's Toe for Luck
cards.subtitle: A pre-exam superstition centered on the Fairfax Campus statue
cards.notes: Pause at the bronze statue and rub the left toe gently for luck before a paper or exam; avoid climbing on the sculpture.
cards.short_summary: Repeated rubbing has made one bronze toe the university's most visible good-luck charm.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason's official traditions page says Fairfax and Songdo students rub the statue's bronze left toe for luck, especially before papers or exams.
cards.access_notes: The tradition is performed at the statue; treat the artwork gently and remain on the surrounding public plaza.

cards.title: Start Mason with George in the Frame
cards.subtitle: A long-running orientation photo ritual at the George Mason Statue
cards.notes: Take an orientation-day portrait in front of George, then save it to pair with a graduation photo at the same landmark.
cards.short_summary: New students mark their arrival with an official orientation portrait beside the university's namesake.
cards.evidence_claim: Mason Orientation calls taking student photos at the George Mason Statue a long-standing Mason tradition and maintains galleries through winter 2026.
cards.access_notes: Orientation uses the Johnson Center as the photo location when weather prevents outdoor statue photos.

cards.title: Dress George for the Occasion
cards.subtitle: Student groups transform the statue for milestones and campus events
cards.notes: Look for George's event-specific outfit, flags, balloons, or graduation cap; photograph the display without moving decorations.
cards.short_summary: The seated bronze George changes appearance as campus groups mark celebrations and milestones.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says student groups decorate the George Mason Statue to advertise activities or commemorate milestones, including spirit events, International Week, and graduation.
cards.access_notes: Decoration is described as a student-group activity; visitors should observe existing displays rather than alter them.

cards.title: Step Around the Unlucky Plaques
cards.subtitle: A four-year-graduation legend embedded at the statue's base
cards.notes: Spot the plaques now embedded in the raised brick base and deliberately step around them while comparing luck rituals with friends.
cards.short_summary: The bad-luck counterpart to the lucky toe warns students away from the plaques beside George.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason's traditions page documents the legend that stepping on either statue plaque could prevent four-year graduation and notes that the plaques are now embedded in the raised base.
cards.access_notes: The plaques are embedded in the statue's raised brick platform, making accidental contact less likely.

cards.title: Paint an Organization's Bench
cards.subtitle: A regulated annual ritual for recognized student organizations
cards.notes: Join your awarded organization's painting team, follow the approved design, and document the finished bench in the SUB I Quad.
cards.short_summary: Recognized organizations renew a colorful, decades-old layer of student identity across the quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Involvement's current Bench Painting Party page provides a 2026 painting schedule and rules for awarded recognized student organizations to paint assigned SUB I Quad benches.
cards.access_notes: Painting is limited to awarded organizations, assigned benches, approved designs, and the official event process.

cards.title: Add Color to the Mason Cubes
cards.subtitle: A generation-to-generation painting tradition on the Fairfax Campus
cards.notes: Seek the campus cubes and photograph their current painted layer; participate only through an authorized student activity.
cards.short_summary: Successive student groups treat the geometric campus objects as a changing, paint-covered record.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason's 2026–2027 New Student Guide lists painting the George Mason cubes among its generation-to-generation traditions.
cards.access_notes: The guide documents the tradition but does not grant unrestricted painting access; use an authorized campus activity.

cards.title: Wear Green and Gold on Friday
cards.subtitle: A weekly display of Patriot colors across campus
cards.notes: Choose George Mason green or gold gear for Friday, then capture a group photo that shows the weekly color tradition in action.
cards.short_summary: A simple Friday wardrobe cue turns the university's colors into a recurring campus-wide ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2026–2027 New Student Guide includes wearing George Mason gear on Fridays in its generation-to-generation traditions list.
cards.access_notes: This is a recurring attire tradition rather than a scheduled or access-controlled event.

cards.title: Turn the Mortarboard into a Message
cards.subtitle: A graduation tradition documented in the current student guide
cards.notes: Plan a cap design that photographs clearly from above, secure every element, and follow current commencement attire guidance.
cards.short_summary: Graduates personalize the square above their gowns with messages, artwork, and markers of their Mason experience.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason's 2026–2027 New Student Guide identifies decorating one's cap for graduation as a generation-to-generation tradition.
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to graduation; students should consult current commencement instructions before decorating regalia.

cards.title: Close the Academic Year at Mason Day
cards.subtitle: George Mason's April carnival tradition before final exams
cards.notes: Watch the official event page for the next date, then plan around rides, games, music, and the available low-stimulus area.
cards.short_summary: The university's longest-running celebration converts the Fairfax Campus into a spring carnival before finals.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason University reports that Mason Day 2026 was its largest and longest-standing tradition, held April 24 with carnival games, rides, food, and music.
cards.source_title: Mason Day 2026: Community, Celebration, and 61 Years of Tradition
cards.access_notes: Mason Day is a scheduled university event; consult the current official page for eligibility, location, and event rules.
